note: Creates the XML reader from the attacker-controlled file input with parsed options and encoding.
Reads through the XML document; during traversal, the reader may free sibling nodes when moving past them.
When the reader moves up from a parent, it frees the last child node if NODE_IS_PRESERVED is not set. This triggers xmlTextReaderFreeProp on the child's attributes.
For an ID attribute being freed during reading, xmlTextReaderRemoveID is called, which sets id->name = attr->name but does NOT remove the entry from the hash table.
The ID entry's name pointer is set to the attribute's name, which is about to be freed. The entry remains in the hash table.
The attribute's name is freed via DICT_FREE. Since the dict does not own the string, xmlFree is called. The ID entry's name now points to freed memory.
When the reader is freed, xmlTextReaderFreeDoc is called on the document.
The ID hash table is freed first, iterating over all remaining entries.
For the stale ID entry whose name was already freed in step 6, xmlFreeID is called.
DICT_FREE tries to free id->name again, which was already freed in step 6. Since the dict does not own the string, xmlFree is called on already-freed memory, causing a heap-double-free crash.
